what: Lumi, a radiant chibi star witch girl (she/her): very long flowing golden-blonde hair with a small dark ribbon, amber-gold eyes, an open-mouthed happy smile; a huge purple witch hat with a wide white-and-gold brim, gold star prints, a gold crescent-moon emblem and tall gold star spikes on the band, and a long floppy purple-and-white striped tip ending in a dangling gold star; small golden feathered wing pauldrons on her shoulders; a white-and-gold armoured dress with a violet star gem on the chest, wide white sleeves, a flowing purple cape with white-and-gold edges and little gold stars dangling from its hem, white-and-gold armoured boots; a long gold spear-staff topped by a bright gold four-pointed star inside two thin crossing pink-and-gold orbit rings, held upright in her hand on the image's right side, with small gold star charms hanging from it; she floats lightly just above the ground, facing right in a 3/4 view
pose: She hovers majestically a little above the ground, her small golden wings spread, holding the galaxy-orbit spear-staff high and forward in her hand on the image's right side so the bright gold star and its two crossing orbit rings shine above her, her other hand open and sweeping outward at her side; a confident radiant smile, cape and long hair flowing behind her.
idle: a slow, gentle floating hover. Face, eyes, body, arms, legs, the spear-staff and the hat brim stay exactly as in Image 1 in every frame. Only these move, each a SMALL step from the previous frame: the long floppy tip of her witch hat swings softly like a slow pendulum (frame 1 rest, frames 2-3 the tip lifts a little, frame 4 highest, frames 5-6 it sinks back past rest, frame 7 lowest, frame 8 halfway back to rest) with its dangling star following and twinkling; the loose ends of her golden hair and the cape hem with its dangling gold stars drift in the same slow wave; the gold star at the spear head glows brighter around frame 4 and dimmer around frame 8 and its two thin orbit rings rotate a little each frame; the small golden wings flutter very slightly. Her hair stays pure golden yellow with clean solid locks: no green tint, no translucent wisps.
fidgets: she rolls the spear-staff between her fingers so it spins on its own long axis like a top, while it stays held at exactly the same place and angle as in Image 1; the two thin orbit rings around its gold star swing around the star like planet orbits, a quarter turn further each frame (frames 2-7), the star flashes brighter with a tiny crisp gold-and-cyan zigzag crackle on it at frames 4-5, and at frame 7 the rings settle back to their tilt in Image 1. Her arm, hand, body, face, hat, cape and hair stay exactly as in Image 1 in every frame. Her hair stays pure golden yellow with clean solid locks: no green tint, no translucent wisps.

she spreads her small golden wings wide and does a happy little twirl in the air: frame 2 wings open and she rises a little, frames 3-5 her body spins once around (side, back, other side) with cape and hair swirling and the spear kept in her hand, frame 6 she faces right again with a joyful smile and wings wide, frame 7 she floats down with the wings folding; same size in every frame. Her hair stays pure golden yellow with clean solid locks: no green tint, no translucent wisps.
entrance: Frame 1: no girl yet, only nine small bright gold stars in a wide ring high in the cell. Frame 2: the nine stars streak inward toward one point above her spot, each with a short solid gold trail. Frame 3: they merge into one blazing gold star. Frame 4: it drops as a huge jagged gold-and-cyan lightning bolt striking her spot from top to bottom, no girl yet. Frame 5: the bolt splits open into a bright pale-gold silhouette of her with wings spread and spear raised. Frame 6: the silhouette becomes the girl in full colour, wings spread wide, cape and hair blown upward, a ring of small gold stars around her feet. Frame 7: she sinks gently into her hover, wings folding to their resting spread, the star ring fading. Frame 8: exactly the resting showcase pose, nothing extra.
